_comment: The topic bank. Each entry must carry `proof` - a specific thing that was
actually built, measured or broken. Content without proof is filler and
converts at zero, however well it is written.

topics.title: Automating a system that has no API, without it breaking every month
topics.intent: Has a legacy web tool to automate and knows Selenium scripts rot.
topics.proof: vTools has no write API; the toolkit uses a `calibrate` step that records real form fields instead of hardcoding selectors, which is why it survives IEEE's form changes.

topics.title: The approval gate: letting an agent touch a live account safely
topics.intent: Wants agent automation but is afraid it will publish something wrong.
topics.proof: Two-phase propose/publish, where phase one physically cannot reach a live system - it writes only to drafts/ and out/ - plus two independent flags off by default.

topics.title: Running an IEEE section event across four platforms from one command
topics.intent: An IEEE officer drowning in vTools, eNotice, WordPress and LinkedIn.
topics.proof: One command produces the vTools event, the eNotice, the website post and the LinkedIn copy with a generated flyer, for the Houston Section.

topics.title: Writing a CLAUDE.md that stops an agent doing the expensive thing
topics.intent: Uses Claude Code and wants the agent to respect real operational rules.
topics.proof: A rules file where the non-negotiables are enforced in code, not prose - publish refuses to run if the three required event contacts are missing.

topics.title: What I refuse to automate, and why that list keeps getting longer
topics.intent: Deciding where the line is between useful automation and liability.
topics.proof: eNotice goes out to the whole section list and cannot be recalled, so it is prepared and never auto-sent. LinkedIn browser automation breaches their user agreement and can get the page restricted.

topics.title: Handling payment webhooks correctly when you are one person
topics.intent: Building a small paid product and worried about double delivery.
topics.proof: HMAC verification with constant-time compare, the signature reused as the dedupe key, and a deliberate 500 on failure so the gateway retries.

topics.title: The volunteer ops problem: why professional societies run on unpaid evenings
topics.intent: A society officer wondering whether the workload is normal.
topics.proof: The concrete per-event task list across four platforms, and how much of it is genuinely mechanical.

topics.title: Running a small business on GitHub Actions and nothing else
topics.intent: Wants automation running on a schedule without paying for a server.
topics.proof: Scheduled workflows as the runtime, secrets in Actions, SQLite as the database, and the specific point where this stops being sufficient.
